Pure Premium Modeling

2026-09-14

Source: https://metricgate.com/blogs/tweedie-glm-insurance-pure-premium/

Data Preprocessing

The given data set has 40,071 rows, but we are told that there are only 10,000 policyholders and 4 different coverage types. Since there’s no duplicated rows, this means there are some policyholders who filed more than one claim. Thus, for policyholders who filed more than one claim per insurance coverage, we need to combine the amount for those claims.

# check if there's any duplicate rows
cat("There are ", sum(duplicated(data)), "duplicated rows.")
## There are  0 duplicated rows.
# converting risk tier into categorical variable
data$risk_tier <- as.character(data$risk_tier)
head(data)
## # A tibble: 6 × 15
##   student_id name   class study   gpa greek off_campus distance_to_campus gender
##        <dbl> <chr>  <chr> <chr> <dbl> <chr> <chr>                   <dbl> <chr> 
## 1          1 Saiz,… Juni… Huma… 1.20  Non-… On campus                   0 Male  
## 2          1 Saiz,… Juni… Huma… 1.20  Non-… On campus                   0 Male  
## 3          1 Saiz,… Juni… Huma… 1.20  Non-… On campus                   0 Male  
## 4          1 Saiz,… Juni… Huma… 1.20  Non-… On campus                   0 Male  
## 5          2 Reddy… Juni… Scie… 0.610 Non-… On campus                   0 Female
## 6          2 Reddy… Juni… Scie… 0.610 Non-… On campus                   0 Female
## # ℹ 6 more variables: sprinklered <lgl>, coverage <chr>, claim_id <dbl>,
## #   amount <dbl>, risk_tier <chr>, training_holdout <chr>
#Combining Multiple Claims made by the same policyholder and coverage
data <- data |>
  group_by(student_id,coverage) |>
  summarize(
    amount= sum(amount, na.rm = TRUE),
    name= first(name),
    class=first(class),
    study=first(study),
    gpa=first(gpa),
    greek= first(greek),
    off_campus= first(off_campus),
    distance_to_campus = first(distance_to_campus),
    gender= first(gender),
    sprinklered =first(sprinklered),
    risk_tier= first(risk_tier),
    training_holdout= first(training_holdout),
    .groups = "drop"
)

head(data)
## # A tibble: 6 × 14
##   student_id coverage            amount name  class study   gpa greek off_campus
##        <dbl> <chr>                <dbl> <chr> <chr> <chr> <dbl> <chr> <chr>     
## 1          1 Additional Living …      0 Saiz… Juni… Huma… 1.20  Non-… On campus 
## 2          1 Guest Medical            0 Saiz… Juni… Huma… 1.20  Non-… On campus 
## 3          1 Liability                0 Saiz… Juni… Huma… 1.20  Non-… On campus 
## 4          1 Personal Property        0 Saiz… Juni… Huma… 1.20  Non-… On campus 
## 5          2 Additional Living …      0 Redd… Juni… Scie… 0.610 Non-… On campus 
## 6          2 Guest Medical            0 Redd… Juni… Scie… 0.610 Non-… On campus 
## # ℹ 5 more variables: distance_to_campus <dbl>, gender <chr>,
## #   sprinklered <lgl>, risk_tier <chr>, training_holdout <chr>
# Grouping the continous variables into 3 bands to make the pricing model easier to rate 
data <- data |>
  mutate(
    gpa_interval= case_when(
      gpa<1 ~ "Sub 1.0",
      gpa<3 ~ "1.0 to 2.99",
      gpa>=3 ~"Greater than 3"
    ),
    
    distance_interval= case_when(
    distance_to_campus==0 ~ "Living On Campus",
    distance_to_campus <=1 ~ "Living 1 mile or less from Campus",
    distance_to_campus > 1 ~ " Living more than 1 mile from Campus"
  )
)

1. Personal Property

Full Model

training <- data |> filter(training_holdout == "training", 
                           coverage == "Personal Property")
holdout <- data |> filter(training_holdout == "holdout",
                          coverage == "Personal Property")
# estimate Tweedie power index p

profile <- tweedie_profile(
  amount ~ risk_tier + study + gpa + greek + off_campus +
    distance_to_campus + gender + sprinklered,
  data = training, p.vec = seq(1.1, 1.6, by = 0.1),
  link.power = 0, do.plot = FALSE
)
## ================================================================================================================================================================================================================================================
p_hat <- profile$p.max
cat("Estimated Tweedie power p:", round(p_hat, 3))
## Estimated Tweedie power p: 1.324
# fits Tweedie GLM w/ log link
personal_prop_full_model <- glm(
  amount ~ risk_tier + study + gpa + greek + off_campus + 
    distance_to_campus + gender + sprinklered,
  data = training,
  family = tweedie(var.power = p_hat, link.power = 0),
  control = glm.control(maxit = 15)
)

summary(personal_prop_full_model)
## 
## Call:
## glm(formula = amount ~ risk_tier + study + gpa + greek + off_campus + 
##     distance_to_campus + gender + sprinklered, family = tweedie(var.power = p_hat, 
##     link.power = 0), data = training, control = glm.control(maxit = 15))
## 
## Coefficients:
##                      Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)          6.574304   0.285527  23.025  < 2e-16 ***
## risk_tier2           0.162276   0.104807   1.548 0.121581    
## risk_tier3           0.016198   0.095658   0.169 0.865541    
## studyHumanities     -0.310407   0.116906  -2.655 0.007942 ** 
## studyOther          -0.149843   0.114728  -1.306 0.191567    
## studyScience        -0.127951   0.113368  -1.129 0.259088    
## gpa                 -0.053366   0.048816  -1.093 0.274337    
## greekNon-greek      -1.505003   0.084336 -17.845  < 2e-16 ***
## off_campusOn campus -0.717487   0.104506  -6.866 7.12e-12 ***
## distance_to_campus   0.009136   0.015790   0.579 0.562870    
## genderFemale        -0.187703   0.232126  -0.809 0.418756    
## genderMale          -0.102724   0.231613  -0.444 0.657405    
## genderOther         -0.273196   0.278625  -0.981 0.326861    
## sprinkleredTRUE     -0.317679   0.086886  -3.656 0.000258 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## (Dispersion parameter for Tweedie family taken to be 284.0655)
## 
##     Null deviance: 937100  on 7998  degrees of freedom
## Residual deviance: 818397  on 7985  degrees of freedom
## AIC: NA
## 
## Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 8
holdout$pred  <- predict(personal_prop_full_model, newdata = holdout, type = "response")

personal_prop_full_avg_amt <- holdout |>
  summarize(observed = mean(amount), 
            fitted = mean(pred),
            abs_difference = abs(observed - fitted))
personal_prop_full_avg_amt
## # A tibble: 1 × 3
##   observed fitted abs_difference
##      <dbl>  <dbl>          <dbl>
## 1     94.1   106.           11.5
col_means <- colMeans(holdout[c("amount", "pred")])

barplot(col_means, 
        col = c("goldenrod1", "royalblue4"),
        main = "Average Personal Property Amount: \n Actual vs. Predicted \n (Full Model)",
        names.arg = c("Actual", "Predicted"), 
        ylim = c(0, 120),
        ylab = "Average Value")

personal_prop_avg_amt <- holdout |>
  group_by(risk_tier) |>
  summarize(observed = mean(amount), 
            fitted = mean(pred),
            abs_difference = abs(observed - fitted))
personal_prop_avg_amt
## # A tibble: 3 × 4
##   risk_tier observed fitted abs_difference
##   <chr>        <dbl>  <dbl>          <dbl>
## 1 1             77.2  100.0           22.8
## 2 2             97.4  123.            25.8
## 3 3            117.   103.            14.2
# barplot to compare actual average claim amount vs average predicted claim amount
personal_prop_avg_amt |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(observed, fitted),
               names_to = "type", values_to = "mean_pp") |>
  mutate(type = factor(type, levels = c("observed", "fitted"),
                       labels = c("Observed", "Fitted"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = risk_tier, y = mean_pp, fill = type)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Observed" = "royalblue4",
                               "Fitted" = "goldenrod1")) +
  labs(title = "Observed vs. Tweedie-fitted \n Average Personal Property Claim Amount (Full Model)",
       x = "Risk Tier", y = "Mean Pure Premium", fill = "")

Variable Selection

Since there are more samples than variables (\(n = 40071 > p = 11\)), we use Backward Stepwise Selection to perform variable selection. We choose a p-value of 0.05 as our cutoff.

Iteration 1

Based on the table below, we should drop the variable distance_to_campus.

# removing 1 variable
drop1(personal_prop_full_model, test = "F")
## Single term deletions
## 
## Model:
## amount ~ risk_tier + study + gpa + greek + off_campus + distance_to_campus + 
##     gender + sprinklered
##                    Df Deviance  F value    Pr(>F)    
## <none>                  818397                       
## risk_tier           2   819128   3.5676 0.0282679 *  
## study               3   820414   6.5603 0.0001998 ***
## gpa                 1   818724   3.1943 0.0739325 .  
## greek               1   905839 853.1586 < 2.2e-16 ***
## off_campus          1   831726 130.0470 < 2.2e-16 ***
## distance_to_campus  1   818494   0.9468 0.3305734    
## gender              3   818958   1.8235 0.1405019    
## sprinklered         1   822149  36.6044 1.512e-09 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
personal_prop_model_1 <- update(personal_prop_full_model, . ~ . - distance_to_campus)
summary(personal_prop_model_1)

Using a p-value cutoff of 0.05, the table below suggests we should stop removing variables. Thus, personal_prop_model_3 is our final model for predicting the expected claim loss for personal property claims.

2. Additional Living Expenses

Full Model

training <- data |> filter(training_holdout == "training", 
                           coverage == "Additional Living Expense")
holdout <- data |> filter(training_holdout == "holdout",
                          coverage == "Additional Living Expense")
# estimate Tweedie power index p

  amount ~ risk_tier + study + gpa + greek + off_campus +
    distance_to_campus + gender + sprinklered,
  data = training, p.vec = seq(1.1, 1.6, by = 0.1),
  link.power = 0, do.plot = FALSE
)
## ================================================================================================================================================================================================================================================
p_hat <- profile$p.max
cat("Estimated Tweedie power p:", round(p_hat, 3))
## Estimated Tweedie power p: 1.335
# fits Tweedie GLM w/ log link
living_exp_full_model <- glm(
  amount ~ risk_tier + study + gpa + greek + off_campus + 
    distance_to_campus + sprinklered + risk_tier,
  data = training,
  family = tweedie(var.power = p_hat, link.power = 0),
  control = glm.control(maxit = 15)
)
holdout$pred  <- predict(living_exp_full_model, newdata = holdout, type = "response")

living_exp_full_avg_amt <- holdout |>
  summarize(observed = mean(amount), 
            fitted = mean(pred),
            abs_difference = abs(observed - fitted))

  mutate(type = factor(type, levels = c("observed", "fitted"),

  ggplot(aes(x = risk_tier, y = mean_pp, fill = type)) +

3. Liability Protection

Full Model

training <- data |> filter(training_holdout == "training", 
                           coverage == "Liability")
holdout <- data |> filter(training_holdout == "holdout",
                          coverage == "Liability")
# estimate Tweedie power index p

profile <- tweedie_profile(
  amount ~ risk_tier + study + gpa + greek + off_campus +
    distance_to_campus + gender + sprinklered,
  data = training, p.vec = seq(1.1, 1.6, by = 0.1),
  link.power = 0, do.plot = FALSE
)
## ================================================================================================================================================================================================================================================
## Warning: glm.fit: algorithm did not converge
p_hat <- profile$p.max
cat("Estimated Tweedie power p:", round(p_hat, 3))
## Estimated Tweedie power p: 1.447
# fits Tweedie GLM w/ log link
liability_full_model <- glm(
  amount ~ risk_tier + study + gpa + greek + off_campus + 
    distance_to_campus + gender + sprinklered,
  data = training,
  family = tweedie(var.power = p_hat, link.power = 0),
  control = glm.control(maxit = 15)
)

summary(liability_full_model)

Final Model

holdout$pred  <- predict(guest_medical_model1, newdata = holdout, type = "response")

guest_medical_avg_amt <- holdout |>
  summarize(observed = mean(amount), 
            fitted = mean(pred),
            abs_difference = abs(observed - fitted))
guest_medical_avg_amt
## # A tibble: 1 × 3
##   observed fitted abs_difference
##      <dbl>  <dbl>          <dbl>
## 1     341.   434.           93.5
col_means <- colMeans(holdout[c("amount", "pred")])

barplot(col_means, 
        col = c("goldenrod1", "royalblue4"),
        main = "Guest Medical Amount: \n Actual vs. Predicted \n (Reduced Model)",
        names.arg = c("Actual", "Predicted"), 
        ylim = c(0, 500),
        ylab = "Average Value")

guest_medical_avg_amt <- holdout |>
  group_by(risk_tier) |>
  summarize(observed = mean(amount), 
            fitted = mean(pred),
            abs_difference = abs(observed - fitted))
guest_medical_avg_amt
## # A tibble: 3 × 4

# barplot to compare actual average claim amount vs average predicted claim amount
guest_medical_avg_amt |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(observed, fitted),
               names_to = "type", values_to = "mean_pp") |>
  mutate(type = factor(type, levels = c("observed", "fitted"),
                       labels = c("Observed", "Fitted"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = risk_tier, y = mean_pp, fill = type)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Observed" = "royalblue4",
                               "Fitted" = "goldenrod1")) +
  labs(title = "Observed vs. Tweedie-fitted \n Average Guest Medical Amount (Full Model)",
       x = "Risk Tier", y = "Mean Pure Premium", fill = "")
